 Vs

full_judgment:
82. Proof of charge of murder must be free from doubt. Mere suspicion cannot be substitute for proof of murder charge. In the case of Swapan vs state reported in 1 MLR 205 their Lordships have held as under:— 

 "There is, no doubt, strong suspicion here and there in the evidence of the PWs to presume that the appellant might have committed the murder. But it is well-settled that suspicion however, strong is not substitute for proof. The mind is apt to pleasure in adopting circumstances to one another and even straining them a little to force them to form parts of one connected whole. We find from the impugned judgment that mind of the learned Additional Sessions Judge reacted in that way and consequently he could not distinguish between the evidence and the suspicion. Thus the impugned conviction cannot be sustained." 

 83. The fundamental principle of a criminal trial is that the accused shall be presumed innocent and that he is not required to adduce evidence to prove his innocence, but the entire burden of proof of his guilt lies on the prosecution alone and till that time the presumption of innocence continues, whether the case is before the trial Court or at higher forums. In this connection reliance may be placed on the case of Muslimuddin vs State reported in 7 BLD (AD) 1 = 38 DLR (AD) 311.
